I’ll trace where per-root type-flow findings are filtered and merged, confirm the ordering bug, then add the two-root regression and keep the fix confined to that merge boundary. I’ll validate the requested suites through a fresh isolated target and commit once in the specified worktree.

The suspected cause is confirmed: `absent_member_findings` applies `finding_proof` inside each root solve, while the pipeline merges rows by `(site, class)` afterward. That lets a Conditional root’s row survive even when another root proves the same pair. I’m moving filtering to the end of the absent-member pipeline step, after strongest-tier merging, and will defer that step’s output cap until after filtering.

The new regression fails on the unfixed code exactly as predicted: `finding_proof: conditional` returns `app.C` at the shared access with `root_parameter`, even though a separate root proves that same pair. I’m now moving selection after the pipeline’s keyed merge; the test’s proven and any checks will pin one Proven row.

The merge fix compiles and the regression now passes its conditional-filter assertion. The focused run stopped on my fixture assertion using the wrong access line (the access is on line 5, not line 2); I’m correcting that test expectation and rerunning it.

The regression now passes: Conditional returns no row, while Proven and Any each return the same single Proven pair. The code now defers proof filtering until the absent-member step has merged all per-root rows; I’m beginning the requested full validation sequence.

Confirmed the bug: proof filtering happened per root before the pipeline merged findings by site and class. The fix applies the filter after merging, then applies the output cap. evidence.user_prompt_tail: tier across all roots in the query. `:proof proven` returns pairs whose strongest tier is Proven; `:proof conditional` returns only pairs whose strongest tier is Conditional; `any` returns each pair once with its strongest tier. Confirm the cause, fix it where the filter and the merge meet (crates/bifrost-rql/src/structural/search/type_flow.rs or wherever the merge lives), and add a regression: two roots reach one access, one with a complete set (Proven) and one with a root_parameter remainder (Conditional); `conditional` returns nothing, `proven` and `any` return one Proven row. Validate: -p brokk-bifrost-rql, -p brokk-bifrost-flow, --test suite_semantic, --test suite_cross_language, --test suite_bench_policy, clippy, fmt, through the isolated-target helper. Another agent is implementing #3759 (collapse of masked repeats) in bifrost5-3759 on top of 94e4f59e7 and touches the same row code; keep your change small. Commit once with a plain-language message. Handback: SHA, confirmed cause, fix location, counts.
